executive_summary:
The host plays a viral clip from Tucker Carlson's interview with Mario Nawfal (A-2646.1). In it Carlson says Dan Bongino told him that Trump shut down the Butler investigation, and that Bongino became "hysterical" when Carlson raised Thomas Matthew Crooks's social media posts, which the public had been told did not exist. The host then plays Bongino's response video (A-2647.1). In it Bongino calls the claim "100% made up" and shows a November 21 Fox News article by Brooke Singman saying the FBI concluded Crooks acted alone and the case sits in "pending inactive" status (A-2647.2). He also shows his texts to Carlson (A-2647.3). The host argues that the November article predates the December conversation Carlson described. She also argues that Bongino's text telling Carlson to ask the president to release "more information" confirms that more information is being withheld. She says she is inclined to believe Butler was a real attempt that served as a "gangster" warning to Trump.

The host next reads a New York Times piece on the White House's handling of the Epstein files (A-2648.1). According to the article, on July 12, 2025 Trump called Charlie Kirk and scolded him after the Turning Point USA Student Action Summit turned into "an Epstein grievance fest." She places this on her timeline (A-2649.1) the day after Tucker Carlson's July 11 summit speech. She then sets Erika Kirk's July 14 Calvary Chapel speech in Long Beach, where Erika spoke after a pro-Israel introduction by James Kaddis (A-2650.1, A-2650.2), against a memory she says she had forgotten. After she taped an interview with Carlson in Maine that July (A-2651.1), the host says, Carlson told her he had just had dinner with Charlie and Erika Kirk and that Erika was "hardcore on the anti-Israel train." The host calls this evidence that Erika Kirk changes her persona by audience, and she revisits the July 18 UVU request, the Yrefy sponsorship, the Hamptons retreat and the Aspen retreat.

The host then turns to Bradley Hansell's September trip on SAM702 (A-2652.1). She says it ran Joint Base Andrews–Colorado Springs–Tucson–Fort Huachuca (September 8)–El Paso, and that the 19-hour stop at Fort Huachuca was the longest. She reads the Department of War FOIA office's reply to her request for the flight's passenger records (A-2653.1). The reply invokes "unusual circumstances", including consultation with other agencies, and places the request in a complex processing queue of about 3,534 open requests. She calls it an "FOFU."

In the final segments the host mocks an X trend summarising Laura Loomer's confrontation with her show (A-2654.1). She replays Erika Kirk's closing remarks at the Women's Leadership Summit after Erika was heckled (A-2655.1) and reads viewer comments (A-2656). She closes by inviting members of Charlie Kirk's family to reach out to her off the record (A-2657.1).

claims.label: Tucker Carlson says Dan Bongino told him Trump shut down the Butler investigation
claims.claim: In a clip from his interview with Mario Nawfal, Tucker Carlson says Trump shut down the investigation into Butler and that Dan Bongino told him so.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the Carlson–Bongino text exchanges Carlson says he still has, and FBI records on the Butler case status after January 2025.

claims.label: Carlson says he obtained Crooks social media posts the FBI said did not exist
claims.claim: Carlson says he came into possession of many social media posts by Thomas Crooks from the months and years before the shooting, which the public had been told did not exist, and that the FBI had lied about this under Christopher Wray.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the posts Carlson holds against FBI public statements on Crooks's online history.
claims.transcript_snippet: accidentally came into possession of a lot of the social media posts that we were told didn't exist that were posted by Thomas Crooks in the months and years before the shooting

claims.label: Bongino told Carlson to "take it up with Trump" in early December
claims.claim: Carlson says that after a long series of texts and calls, Bongino told him to take it up with Trump because Trump had shut down the investigation, in about the first or second week of December.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the December call and text records between Carlson and Bongino.
claims.transcript_snippet: he said, "Look, take it up with Trump. He's the one who shut down the investigation." And that was, I think, the first or second week of December.

claims.label: Host says the Butler story terrified Dan Bongino and Kash Patel
claims.claim: Recapping Tucker Carlson's account that he asked Dan Bongino and Kash Patel why the public was told Thomas Matthew Crooks had no social media history, the host says the Butler story, "perhaps the butler cover up", terrified Bongino and Patel.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Carlson's full account and Bongino's response; compare FBI statements on Crooks's online history against what was later disclosed.
claims.transcript_snippet: this story, the butler story, perhaps the butler cover up, whatever it is, terrified Dan Bonino and terrified Kash Patel.

claims.label: Bongino says the claim that Trump shut down the Butler investigation is made up
claims.claim: In his response video, Dan Bongino says Carlson's statement that the president shut down the Butler investigation is "Totally, completely 100% made up."
